title: Sample 15-9: Marginal Numbers Indicating Words Read

illustrates.quote: 15.8.1 Word counts are used for timed readings and typing tests. The numbers fall at the end of the print line. a. Treat counted words as line-numbered text, leaving three spaces at the end of each line of text. b. Insert a transcriber’s note explaining the use of the three blank cells, and that the number refers to the end of the print line. Sample: Three blank cells indicate the end of a print line. The numbers in the right margin are the number of words read at the point of the three blank cells. c. Insert a blank line between the transcriber’s note and the beginning of the line-numbered material.

blocks.features: A large reversed-out (white-on-black) block containing the numeral 7, printed beside the title — both runs agree this is omitted from the braille transcription; not modeled.

blocks.text: The Rat That Had a Fast Rate
Sandy had a rat that ate fast. She said, “That rat eats too
much. I must make the rat slow down.”
Sandy went to the store and got ten packs of gum. She said,
“I will smear the gum on the oats.” Then she gave the oats to
the rat. “Here are some oats,” she said. “You will have fun
blocks.features: The word 'fun' is underlined in print (omitted here — not modeled by buildModel15, no other file in this section carries emphasis on numbered-text words).

print.notes: This rule's numbers are cumulative WORD counts (words read so far), not sequential print-line numbers — confirmed both by the print image (every line prints its own running count) and by direct decode of the given braille's own right-margin digits (13, 21, 34, 48, 60, 62), which already match exactly what both runs originally supplied; unlike every other file in this section, no interpolation was needed here since print itself already numbers every single line. No explicit transcriber's-note print.blocks entry is modeled (see the same reasoning as Sample 15-3's own README/notes): the note in the gold braille below is 15.8.1b's own suggested wording, used here to test Emboss's automatic line-numbered-text note against the book's own worked illustration of the correct wording.
print.printFeatures: Word counts printed in the right margin at the end of every line, representing the total words read so far (a timed-reading/typing-test passage, 15.8.1).
